approach: Put the rule in one place in athena-git: `Git::own_origin_url(remote)` refuses any remote name but `origin`, requires `git remote get-url --all origin` and `git remote get-url --push --all origin` to each list exactly one URL, and requires both to name the same repository (userinfo, scheme, `.git`, trailing slash and scp-style colon normalised away). `Git::push_branch` and `Git::push_if_remote_at` call it first. In crates/athena-core/src/gh/remote.rs add `guard_origin_write(git, name)`, which wraps it, and call it first in `GitRemote::push`, `replace` and `delete_branch`; reads (`remote_head`, `commits_after`) stay unguarded. The pull-request side is pinned the same way: `land_pr` (landing.rs:866-867) and `Athena::github_repository` (early.rs:363-366) read the origin URL through the checked read, so the `GhClient` repository comes from the single validated origin and a doubled or mismatched origin yields no host call. Tests use real git against temp bare `origin` and `upstream` repos; each first shows a plain `git push` to `upstream` succeeds (same user, same environment), then shows the guarded call refused with refs unchanged. docs/spec.toml gets the mechanism and a measure ending `status: not shown`; CHANGELOG.md gets one Unreleased line.

decisions.choice: Put the URL check in `athena_git::Git::own_origin_url` (athena-git/src/lib.rs) and have remote.rs `guard_origin_write` call it.
decisions.reason: athena-core depends on athena-git (system facts crate reach), not the reverse, and the records writer pushes through `Git::push_branch`/`push_if_remote_at` (records_branch.rs:442-444), which core's GitRemote never sees. One implementation covers both paths and criterion 2 names both files.

rejected.why: Records pushes (append_to_remote, athena-gate attribution.rs:1160/1612, athena-cli main.rs:1751) would stay able to push to any named remote, so Athena's own publishing would not be bounded.

rejected.option: Duplicate the check in core and git
rejected.why: Two copies of a URL-identity rule can drift; one function is easier to show with a test.

decisions.choice: Refuse when `get-url --all` or `get-url --push --all` lists more than one URL, or when the two name different repositories. Error text never echoes a URL.
decisions.reason: A push goes to every push URL (the push URLs, else the fetch URLs); a doubled push URL, or a doubled fetch URL with no push URL, would publish to a second place. `get-url --push --all` falls back to the fetch URLs, so one pair of reads covers both cases. parse_remote's comment (client.rs:1194-1195) says URLs are not echoed because they may carry a credential.

rejected.why: It returns the first URL only; it misses a second push URL and a separate push URL.
Local-path origins (every test) are not GitHub URLs and parse_remote would reject them. The guard must work for any URL form, so it uses a generic normalisation.

decisions.choice: The guard allows exactly the name `origin` and does not look for a separate list of allowed remotes.
decisions.reason: The brief's rule is 'the repo's own origin'; every production caller already passes the literal origin (landing.rs:865, early.rs:374-377 and 458-461, reconcile.rs:403, cli main.rs:1751), so no caller changes behavior.

rejected.option: A config key listing allowed remotes
rejected.why: It would touch athena.toml or defaults.toml, which are out of scope, and would let a setting widen the boundary.

decisions.choice: Test the land_pr ordering with a source-order assertion on landing.rs (the checked origin read comes before `GitRemote {` and `GitLandingRecords::for_remote`), plus a direct test of the helper that read uses. Real enforcement stays in the recheck inside GitRemote and Git.
decisions.reason: A full `Athena::land_pr` run needs a verified job and records worktree; existing land_pr tests with such a job go through `Rig` and `FakeRemote`, which would hide the lookup. A no-origin call to the helper and to GitRemote shows the refusal for real; the text assertion pins only the order.

rejected.option: Build a verified job in a temp repo and call Athena::land_pr with no origin
rejected.why: Heavy setup for a property the first line of the origin read already decides; the recheck in GitRemote and the helper test show the behavior.

decisions.choice: Do not change reconcile.rs, run/mod.rs `github_origin`, or `rebase_job_branch`.
decisions.reason: They read only: reconcile's host calls are reads and its record writes go through the guarded push_branch/push_if_remote_at; run/mod.rs:1737 feeds a CI read; rebase_job_branch (landing.rs:761-827) 'never pushes'. They are not in the deliverables.

rejected.option: Route reconcile's get-url through the checked read as well
rejected.why: reconcile.rs is not a listed deliverable and the writes it triggers are already refused by the git-level guard.

decisions.choice: For criterion 6, name what the full-workspace run fails on without the behavior: the new guard tests (criteria 3-5) and the two existing pushurl tests are part of `cargo test --locked`, so a missing or mis-wired guard makes that run red, and a wrongly formatted or lint-failing change makes fmt or clippy red.
decisions.reason: The finding asked for a fails_without on criterion 6. The run is the gate for the whole change, so its failure modes are the new refusal tests plus the existing tests that reach the changed push paths.

rejected.option: Leave criterion 6 as an existing-suite run with no failure case
rejected.why: Athena refuses a behavior demonstration with no fails_without.

A twin test in athena-git/src/lib.rs does the same through `Git::push_branch` and `Git::push_if_remote_at`.
